testAreas.access: No role or sign-in restriction was found.
testAreas.setup: Prepare URL inputs and a consuming integration that can call the exported URL utilities; no accounts or other test data are specified.
checks: Verify parsing a URL with ?k=one&k=two retains both values for k as an ordered array rather than returning only two.
Check query encoding for a value containing a space and a literal plus, such as a + b, produces a+b%2B+b while preserving the distinction between the space and plus.
Confirm constructing a URL from an already-parsed URL object is rejected with a TypeError, while string input can be parsed and serialized.

why: None of the checks use a lowercase percent-encoding, and the report never mentions percent-encoding normalization.

report.summary: URL parsing, query handling, and URL composition have been reorganized, changing how some inputs are accepted and serialized.
keyChanges: Repeated query keys can now be represented as multiple values, while query, path, and hash text is encoded and decoded through the URL utilities; blank values can affect how repeated keys are retained.
URL creation now requires string input, whereas the previous parsing flow accepted a parsed-URL object; passing that object now raises a TypeError.
qaChecks: Verify parsing the query string ?tag=&tag=blue retains both tag values, including the initially blank value, rather than dropping or replacing one.
Check URL creation with a previously accepted parsed-URL object containing a URL and protocol metadata; it should now raise a TypeError rather than accept the object.
Confirm query values containing a space and a literal plus sign remain distinguishable in the serialized URL, with the space represented as + and the literal plus encoded as %2B.
uncertainty: No application pages or intended rule for repeated query keys with an initially blank value are supplied, so the expected user-facing behavior for that input is unclear.

report.summary: URL parsing, query handling, and URL construction have been reorganized, with no application-specific surfaces identified for testing.
keyChanges: URL parsing now handles inputs without a protocol directly, so relative paths can be parsed with their query and fragment instead of failing in the parser.
Query strings are now represented separately from paths and parsed into values that retain repeated keys, affecting URL query reading and serialization.
qaChecks: Verify that parsing the relative input "/guide?mode=brief#top" returns the path, query, and fragment without an error; a relative input took a different path before this change.
Check that parsing "/guide?tag=one&tag=two" retains both values for the repeated tag key.
uncertainty: No application pages, API endpoints, or navigation paths are supplied, so the available checks are limited to the URL capabilities shown in the change evidence.

report.summary: The release changes URL parsing, query handling, and normalization through a replacement of the existing URL utilities.
keyChanges: Repeated query keys are now preserved as arrays when parsed, and array values are emitted as repeated key-value pairs when formatting URLs.
URL normalization no longer supports stripping the base from an absolute URL, and inputs previously accepted as parsed URL objects must now be strings.
qaChecks: Verify parsing ?tag=red&tag=blue preserves both tag values as red and blue, rather than returning only blue.
Check formatting a URL with tag values red and blue produces two query pairs, tag=red and tag=blue.
Check normalizing https://example.test/a with the former base-stripping option enabled returns the full absolute URL rather than only /a.
Verify passing a parsed URL object for https://example.test/a is rejected with a TypeError instead of being accepted as URL input.
uncertainty: The supplied context does not establish whether removing base stripping and parsed-object input support is intended compatibility behavior.

report.summary: This release replaces the previous URL handling with a new URL and query-string model, changing parsing behavior and the package’s public exports.
keyChanges: URLs without a protocol now take the path-parsing route instead of the previous absolute-URL parsing route, affecting how relative inputs and their query and hash parts are handled.
The package entry point now exports the new URL and query utilities instead of the previous URL module, which may affect consumers of the prior public exports.
qaChecks: Verify the input /docs?mode=compact#top is accepted as a relative URL and retains its path, query, and hash when read or serialized.
Confirm the input foo-bar://host/path?x=1 retains the foo-bar scheme and host rather than being interpreted as a relative path.
Check that the package entry point exposes the new URL and query utilities and no longer exposes the previous URL module.
uncertainty: The new scheme check does not recognize hyphens in schemes, unlike the previous parser; it is unclear whether treating foo-bar://host/path as a relative path is intentional.

report.summary: The release replaces the previous URL and query handling with a new URL representation and changes which utilities the package exposes.
keyChanges: Query parsing now skips parameters with empty names, so an input such as /path?=value no longer retains that parameter.
URL inputs are recognized as protocol-based only when the scheme contains word characters, so some previously accepted schemes are instead treated as paths.
The package entry point now exports URL and query utilities instead of the previous UFO utility.
qaChecks: Verify that parsing /path?=value skips the query parameter with an empty name.
Check that parsing my-scheme://example.test/path?x=1 treats the input as a path rather than recognizing my-scheme as a protocol.
uncertainty: The evidence shows that schemes containing a hyphen are no longer recognized as protocols, but does not establish whether support for those schemes is expected.
